tools.name: estimate_fit
tools.description: Will this Hugging Face repo run on this hardware? Checks the repo and its quantized derivatives (GGUF/MLX/AWQ...) and returns, per candidate: verdict (fits | fits-tight | offload | no | unknown), memory placement (VRAM / RAM / SSD), longest context that fits, decode and prefill tok/s bands with basi

tools.name: compare_hardware
tools.description: Run one repo against several devices and return the best candidate per device (verdict, quant, decode band, max context, launch command), sorted best first. Use for 'which of my machines should run X' or 'is a 4090 or an M4 Max better for X'. hardware: comma-separated list of presets / free text / c

tools.name: find_models
tools.description: Recommend models for a task on given hardware, written as a natural question, e.g. 'best coding model for an RTX 4090 + 64GB RAM at 32k context', 'Japanese chat on a Galaxy S25 Ultra', 'serve 8 users on 2x RTX 3090'. Ranks indexed Hub models (~20k, refreshed nightly) by fit, task benchmark percentil

tools.name: ask
tools.description: Free-form question about running Hugging Face models locally or self-hosted (runtimes, quant choice, KV cache, why something OOMs, MoE offload); returns markdown plus the parsed query and notes.

tools.name: search_models
tools.description: Search the model index by name without estimating (fast): ids, task, library, params, downloads, likes, license, created date, gated. query: words that must all appear in the repo id, any order, case-insensitive, '-_.' optional; family, uploader, quant method or org/name all work ('qwen3', 'gemma-4'

tools.name: list_hardware
tools.description: List hardware presets (330+: GPUs of every vendor and segment, multi-GPU nodes, Apple, Jetson/APUs, phones, tablets, SBCs, VPS tiers). filter: words matched against id/name/vendor/segment, e.g. 'h100', 'amd datacenter', 'phone samsung', 'vps'. Returns id, name, kind, memory, bandwidth, backend; offs

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "estimate_fit" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
